title: Magic: The Gathering release schedule 2026-2027
content:
What is the current MTG release schedule? This guide tracks all of the upcoming MTG releases in 2026-2027, including release dates, mechanics, and story details. This year, we have crossovers with Star Trek and the Hobbit left, plus a 'What If?' set shaking up the multiverse.

Then in 2027, we're going to a new ocean plane, seeing a massive battle between mechs and monsters on Kamigawa, and finally we get more than a glimpse at what's been going on in Zhalfir.

While you're filling in your calendar, our complete history of all MTG sets in order of release might come in useful too. Below we've collected all the available Magic: The Gathering release dates and windows for 2026 - starting with the upcoming releases, then moving on to the most recent.

Here's the Magic: The Gathering 2026/2027 release schedule:

  • Lorwyn Eclipsed - January 23, 2026
  • Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles - March 6, 2026
  • Secrets of Strixhaven - April 24, 2026
  • Marvel Superheroes - June 26, 2026
  • The Hobbit - August 14, 2026
  • Reality Fracture - October 2, 2026
  • Star Trek - November 11, 2026
  • Mystery Booster Commander Edition - November(?) 2026
  • Nauctis: The Sunken Realm - February 5, 2027
  • Kamigawa: Titanbreach - June 4, 2027
  • Zhalfir - October 1, 2027

Upcoming set release dates

The Hobbit - August 14, 2026

There wasn't enough content in The Hobbit for a satisfying film trilogy, but there's probably enough to make a strong card set. This set features plenty of new versions of characters we've seen before - such as Gandalf, Bilbo, Gollum, and Elrond -and important reprints like Tom Bombadil and The One Ring are reappearing as box-toppers.

There's lots of new stuff to be excited about too, though. Dwarves are making a big appearance - a fantasy race that's oft-ignored by Magic lore. Smaug is also here with several different commanders that are all terrifying treasure-makers, and the stone trolls have a surprisingly powerful card too.

Given how successful the Lord of the Rings set was, I'm sure WotC has high hopes for this release.

Reality Fracture - October 2, 2026

Reality Fracture is a What If? set, where we get to see alternate versions of existing characters. Prepare to meet a fiery Ajani, ice Chandra, Benalian healer Liliana, and chain-veil wielding Garruk. They all hail from an Echoverse created by Jace, who has finally tipped over into full-blown villain.

It's not just the planeswalkers. There are opposite versions of characters and creatures too. Instead of Tinybones there's Titanbones. Instead of Craterhoof, there's a red Craterclaw that cares about artifacts.

The set takes place on Hexhaven, a more combat-focused version of Strixhaven, where Jace has control and seemingly rules with an iron fist, with his own faceless enforcers and eyeball-creature sentinels.

Wizards has done the impossible and included regular and Echoverse versions of the same character in each pack so you can see the change.

Star Trek - November 20, 2026

There are seven Standard-legal sets this year, good grief! There have been rumors of a Star Trek set swirling around for years, and it looks like WotC has finally decided to… make it so.

2026 marks Star Trek's 60th anniversary, and this release will explore the entire history of the show, in its every iteration. It'll be a good time for the Spacecraft mechanic from EOE to return, and we expect to see phasers that dish out stun counters, please and thank you.

Magic has already proven it can jump genres and tackle sci-fi settings, and Star Trek certainly has enough content to produce a working set. That said, the whole ethos of Star Trek seems kind of antithetical to a combat-based TCG. Not to mention: those planeswalkers are violating the Prime Directive all the time.

Mystery Booster: Commander Edition - November 2026

A surprise latecomer to the 2026 release schedule, Mystery Booster: Commander Edition seems designed to delight EDH fans with unlikely throwbacks like a new Joven card, as well as weird and wacky rulebreaker commanders. There are eight of these in total, and each one lets players bend the commander deckbuilding rules in unique ways - such as adding instants and sorcery cards of an additional color.

Like past Mystery Boosters, this set is designed to be drafted. And like past Mystery Boosters, it'll be available at MagicCons or as Festivals in a Box.

On that note, there's an extra MagicCon next year, as the show is showing up in Tokyo for the first time. Here's the 2027 MagicCon schedule:

  • MagicCon Detroit: February 26 - 28
  • MagicCon Tokyo: May 14 - 16
  • MagicCon Las Vegas: August 27 - 29
  • MagicCon Amsterdam: December 3 - 5
1/4

Nauctis: The Sunken Realm - February 5, 2027

The first new set of 2027 takes us under the sea and to a brand new plane. Nauctis: The Sunken Realm explores a water world and takes place entirely beneath the wave. While sea creatures are usually Blue's domain, this fishy focus allows Wizards to flesh out a full color pie of marine life.

You can expert merfolk galore, but also some more unusual fantasy races like puffer fish people, penguin people, crab men, walrus women, and something that I would swear was an underwater sliver, if it didn't have the wrong number of limbs.

WotC is leaning hard into high fantasy with Nauctis, which should be exciting for anyone tiring of all the genre exploration of recent years. Kelp takes the place of forests, there's a new sea-based evasion mechanic that's equivalent to flying, and all the humans are stuck in diving suits and submarines.

All the sea creatures make it a great set for biology nerds too. For instance, there are undead monsters based on whalefall!

1/3

Kamigawa Titanbreach - June 4, 2027

Worlds are at war. Ikoria has collided with Kamigawa, and it's time for an inter-planar showdown. As soon as Wizards started linking planes with Omenpaths, we knew it was only a matter of time before we got a 'Pacific Rim' set, and the hype for Kamigawa: Titanbreach is immediately off the chain. Big mechs, big monsters, two beloved Magic settings shown off to their fullest. What's not to like?

I only have two questions. Is this where we'll finally see Battles make their return? And why did they lead with Aetherdrift instead of this?

Zhalfir - October 1, 2027

Zhalfir is a setting we've been eagerly waiting to see, ever since it phased back into existence at the end of March of the Machine. Now it's getting its own set, providing a fresh take on an old Magic: The Gathering setting.

Longtime players will no doubt find some things familiar about Zhalfir - for instance, a new Teferi legendary creature card is all but guaranteed. However, this is a deeper look at Zhalfir than we ever got when it was part of Dominaria, promising Magic's take on African culture and mythology.

Zhalfir has replaced Mirrodin/New Phyrexia, and it's lit by Mirrodin's five suns, which makes it a land of endless day. Contrasting that is a spirit realm, a dark land full of danger but also a connection to your ancestors. Overall Zhalfir promises to be a visually stunning new world with amazing architecture and fashion - and great hair!

Latest releases in 2026

Lorwyn Eclipsed - January 23, 2026

Lorwyn Eclipsed was the first set of 2026, a long-awaited return to this Celtic folklore inspired world that's every bit as beloved as Kamigawa or Tarkir. That title is a reference to the new identity of the plane. While the twin realities of Lorwyn and Shadowmoor used to alternate every 300 years, they've now fused together.

While Lorwyn is a land of eternal day and flower-filled meadows, Shadowmoor is one of endless night. This set showed off the setting in its new, combined state: part-spooky, part-nice, with its denizens shifting between two forms as the borders of the two worlds constantly move. To show that duality, Lorwyn Eclipsed is full of double-faced cards that you can pay mana to transform.

This release maintained a lot of what fans love about this MTG plane, namely the non-human races of the kithkin, faeries, elves, and merfolk. There are even a few Kindred spells!

Interestingly, this set also introduced us to the new first-year characters from Strixhaven. Are they this phase's protagonists?

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles - March 6, 2026

Revealed slightly later than the rest of the 2026 calendar, the second release of the year was MTG Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. Featuring all your favorite heroes and villains, from Krang to April O'Neil, there's some fun stuff in here - including art from the original comic books and lands based on pizza toppings. It did put me off cheese for at least a week, though.

This was a smaller set, like the Spider-Man release that got such a frosty reception last year. However, the TMNT set came with more interesting side products, including a single five-color Commander precon (here's a handy upgrade guide for you) and a new 'Turtle Team Up' box that provides a cooperative way to play Magic.

Secrets of Strixhaven - April 24, 2026

Secrets of Strixhaven was our second look at this magical school, and featured the five distinct colleges once again - each of which had its own precon. This set introduces some new characters enrolling in the academy, and follows up on the fan-favorites who've just graduated.

While Secrets didn't try to reinvent the mold, it did see us step outside the walls of Strixhaven for the first time. Instead of moving back home to save on rent or cramming like sardines into a shared apartment, the new graduates were using their arcane skills to explore the wider world of Arcavios and broker magical peace treaties.

Secrets of Strixhaven also launched alongside a novel by Seanan Mcguire - the first Magic book in a long while!

Marvel Superheroes - June 26, 2026

Marvel Superheroes launched right as Summer kicked into gear. Perhaps the largest of several planned Magic: The Gathering Marvel sets, it seems Wizards of the Coast has packed in as many characters as they can, from the Avengers, to The Fantastic Four, to Daredevil. And of course, Squirrel Girl is making an appearance for the squirrel tribal lovers.

There's also a Jumpstart release for this set: themed packs that players can mash together into an instant deck. As both UB and Jumpstart are aimed at new players, WotC is experimenting with combining the two concepts.

Marvel Super Heroes is out in the wild now, with dozens of legendary creatures doing super-powered battle, from Marvel greats like Iron Man to obscure heroes like Reptil. In fact, there are so many characters here that honestly we have to wonder what's been left on the table for future releases. We were guessing X-Men would be coming in 2027, but this set features Wolverine, Storm, and Quicksilver.

Another new development for this set is that it's playable on Arena! Seems Wizards renegotiated its deal with Marvel, allowing now the Marvel cards to join Magic's digital platform in a Snap. Ahem

If you're into more than just trading card games, then we can tell you what other products Wizards of the Coast is releasing this year. Head to our DnD release schedule guide for the latest on the world's biggest tabletop RPG.

title: The best MTG Commanders 2026
content:
The Commander is the legendary creature that leads your other 99 cards into battle in games of EDH: they dictate the colors you can include in your deck, and shape your overall strategy. If you're shopping for new options, our tried-and-tested guide to the best MTG commanders recommends plenty that reliably secure wins and are extremely fun to play.

Wizards of the Coast introduces more legendary creatures with each year of new MTG sets, but this guide will help you keep up with the latest releases and meta shifts. If you want to get really competitive, you'll be better served by our dedicated cEDH tier list. Or, if you're just starting out with this format, we'd recommend starting out with MTG commander precon decks instead.

Top commanders MTG:

  • Atraxa, Praetors' Voice
  • Edgar Markov
  • Vivi Ornitier
  • Teval, the Balanced Scale
  • Baylen, the Haymaker
  • The Necrobloom
  • Kenrith, The Returned King
  • Muldrotha, The Gravetide
  • Tymna The Weaver
  • The Gitrog Monster
  • Isshin, Two Heavens As One
  • Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow
  • Sauron, The Dark Lord
  • The Ur Dragon
  • Kaalia Of The Vast
  • Lathril, Blade Of The Elves
  • Pantlaza, Sun Favored
  • Shroofus Sproutshire
  • Atraxa, Grand Unifier

Atraxa, Praetors' Voice

While not quite the dominant force she was in 2016, Atraxa, Praetors' Voice still makes for a top commander. Her proliferate ability opens up all kinds of avenues and has only gotten more flexible as Wizards experiments with new types of counters like shield and stun.

Atraxa is a really great commander to experiment with because her ability and color identity mean you can explore about six different themes. You could make a pretty standard +1/+1 counter deck, or go the opposite route with -1/-1 counters. You could be really unpleasant and run with poison counters, or create a superfriends deck full of planeswalkers.Whatever route you go, you're probably going to want more effects that proliferate, so cards like Ezuri, Stalker of Spheres and Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus are a perfect fit. They also often lend themselves to a Phyrexian theme!

Game Changers for Atraxa, Praetor's Voice

  • Fierce Guardianship
  • Force of Will

Edgar Markov

The Commander 2017 set was all about tribal decks, each focused on a single creature type: cats, wizards, dragons, and vampires. Edgar Markov led the cats - no, sorry, the vampires deck - and quickly rose to the status of top commander. While the card got horribly pricey as a result, a reprint in Innistrad Remastered has made him a little less silly to buy.

With the ability to create a swarm of little nippers, then pump them up each time he attacks, Edgar naturally works best in a horde-style deck that can swiftly overwhelm opponents. Mardu colors give you access to all the top removal cards, and best of all, Edgar's eminence ability makes him useful from the command zone, where he can churn out mini-mes in safety.

You then need stuff to do with all your vampire tokens, like buffing them up or sacrificing them for card draw with Skullclamp and draining your opponent with Blood Artist.

Game Changers for Edgar Markov

  • Braids, Cabal Minion

Vivi Ornitier

MTG's Final Fantasy set was stuffed with legendary creatures, but Vivi Ornitier is the real standout for Commander players. He grows more powerful every time you cast a non-creature spell, and that power in turn fuels an incredibly versatile mana-making ability.

Vivi can be hard to keep in play due to his notoriety (he did terrible things in Standard) but on the bright side, his mana cost is so low that it shouldn't be too hard to bring him back. Keep him on the board long enough, and Vivi becomes a powerful attacker in his own right, but his real value lies in the win conditions you can create with the killer combination of free mana and pinging. A Curiosity-type card also makes this guy a card draw machine.

With Vivi, your game plan might be a spellslinger or storm build - setting up until the perfect turn allows you to combo off. Alternatively, you could go all in on pingers, and aim to whittle your opponents down with a million tiny cuts.

Game Changers for Vivi

  • Cyclonic Rift
  • Mystical Tutor
  • Rhystic Study

Teval, the Balanced Scale

Teval, the Balanced Scale offers fantastic value, especially for a precon commander. This spicy spirit dragon has seen its popularity soar since Tarkir: Dragonstorm, and no wonder. It's a consistent source of land and tokens whose self-mill strategies synergize with a variety of decks.

Obviously, a straightforward graveyard deck is the first place to go. You want cards entering and leaving your graveyard as often as possible to trigger Teval's ability. After that though, you could consider a lands-matter sub-theme, playing multiple lands a turn to stack up the triggers. You could look to get the most from your tokens with zombie tribal cards too.

Your biggest problem will be defending Teval, who has no protection against removal, will suffer when cards are exiled, and who must constantly jump into the fray of battle.

Gamechangers for Teval

  • Force of Will
  • Fierce Guardianship
  • Gifts Ungiven

Baylen, the Haymaker

If you love using tokens, Baylen, the Haymaker might just be the best commander in all of Magic: The Gathering history, but he has surprising depth - this isn't just your typical go-wide tokens leader.

You wouldn't necessarily know that from the first step of your gameplan though: you begin by amassing a token army. They don't all have to be creatures, you can use treasure or food as well. But after this step is where the rabbit is flexible.

If you want to win with commander damage, you can tap your tokens to buff Baylen up with counters and swing for lethal. He turns four tokens into three +1/+1 counters, so even without built-in protection, this is very doable.

Alternatively, you can use your tokens for mana and card draw. That lets you dig through your deck and cast other key pieces that will help you convert tokens into victory.

I'll lastly add that there are few better commanders to pick for an Hare Apparent deck, if you just want to overwhelm your foes with a lupine legion.

Gamechangers for Baylen

  • Smothering Tithe
  • Biorhythm
  • Aura Shards

The Necrobloom

The Necrobloom is easy for opponents to underestimate. On its early turns, it doesn't seem to achieve much - play a land, fetch a land, create a puny plant token. However, if left undisturbed for long enough, it's landfall antics will start to cause serious problems.

As soon as seven types of land are under your control, you can start building a zombie army, all while blocking with your chunky commander their numerous plant buddies. Dredge is on hand to bring back any crucial lands, and it opens up plenty of interactions that keep The Necrobloom's tokens-and-landfall schtick feeling interesting.

Mass land-reanimation is particularly deadly in this deck, creating a huge horde that has to be dealt with in one turn cycle, else it's game over.

Gamechangers for the Necrobloom

  • Field of the Dead
  • Crop Rotation

Kenrith, The Returned King

Five-color commanders are some of the strongest because they allow you to use any card in the game. That means ultimate flexibility. As a result, they're a little controversial, since many lend themselves to less focused strategies and decks, where you just want to cram in all the best cards in your collection.

But we think that's as valid a playstyle as any - and it's hard to pass up jack-of-all-trades commanders when they're as good as Kenrith, the Returned King. Kenrith shines because all of his abilities are useful, and some are invaluable. You only need white mana to cast him, so you can have him out on the field and gradually unlock new abilities as you play new lands.

He's a top commander for those still learning how to play Magic The Gathering's most popular format, since you can experiment to your heart's content, and it's hard to go too wrong. Synergy is not required - just brute strength!

Gamechangers for Kenrith

  • Coalition Victory
  • Gifts Ungiven
  • Fierce Guardianship

Muldrotha, The Gravetide

Do you hate it when your opponents blow up your stuff? Then Muldrotha, the Gravetide is the top commander for you. Allowing you to play one card of each permanent type from your graveyard each and every turn, this noxious elemental turns your graveyard into an extension of your hand.

Unfortunately, with a high cost and incredible ability, Muldrotha is one of those commanders that attracts removal like a magnet. On the bright side, her Sultai colors (black, green and blue) give you access to a ton of power outside of her own impressive strength, including excellent creatures, removal, and card draw.

And when you do manage to protect her for long enough to make good use of her resurrection powers, your opponents are going to have a bad time.

Gamechangers for Muldrotha

  • Gifts Ungiven
  • Intuition
  • Fierce Guardianship

Tymna The Weaver

Tymna the Weaver may not look like much from the outset - sure, she draws cards when you hit people, whatever. But never underestimate the power of friendship. Tymna is a top commander choice because she has the Partner ability, which - like Tymna herself - was introduced in the Commander 2016 set. That means you can pair her up with any legendary creature that also has 'Partner' to give them joint leadership of your commander deck.

Two commanders are better than one, since they unlock new card options and new synergies, as well as ensuring you always have a creature to play out. Tymna makes this list simply because she's one of the most versatile creatures with the Partner ability. The card draw she provides will be valuable, whatever strategy you're going for.

Tymna the Weave is most often paired up with the merfolk card Thrasios, Triton Hero. That's because this combination gives you access to four colors and two commanders with generically powerful abilities. They don't make Partners like this anymore, and for good reason.

Gamechangers for Tymna

  • Thassa's Oracle
  • Orcish Bowmasters

The Gitrog Monster

A froggy chap with a winning smile, The Gitrog Monster has a series of unique, versatile abilities that make for a powerful MTG commander. It lets you play more lands, allowing for copious ramping, and you get to draw cards each time you put lands in the graveyard.

Cards like Crucible of Worlds will help you bring valuable lands back to the battlefield so you can sacrifice them again and again for endless utility. Even a simple Evolving Wilds can be extremely useful for Gitrog.

Whether you're using discard outlets or sacrificing lands, there's plenty of ways to generate absurd value with this top commander. You can also abuse infinite combos, which makes The Gitrog Monster a viable combo deck in cEDH.

Gamechangers for the Gitrog Monster

  • Crop Rotation
  • Field of the Dead
  • Glacial Chasm

Isshin, Two Heavens As One

Isshin, Two Heavens as One has just one simple ability, but its elegance and simplicity belies its power. This high tech samurai doubles up all your attack triggers, letting you generate absurd value whenever you swing at your opponents.

Not the best commander for anyone who likes playing a slower, defensive game, Isshin wants you to strike hard and strike fast. While all Isshin decks want to attack, this is another commander that you can build in a few ways, as there are loads of strong creature cards to choose from, and plenty of room for building up subthemes.

Even better, his very affordable mana cost means you don't have to worry too much about removal spells, as you can play Isshin, Two Heavens as One several times without it becoming too taxing.

Gamechangers for Isshin

  • The One Ring
  • Jeska's Will
  • Teferi's Protection

Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow

If you like ninjas, then Magic: The Gathering has a brilliant commander option. With Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow, your whole deal is striking with low-cost, evasive creatures, then launching your commander into play with ninjitsu, and reaping the rewards: plenty of card draw, and plenty of pain.

The best thing about Yuriko is, as long as you have an unblocked creature, you can always get her into play for two mana. This is huge. It means no matter how many times your opponents deal with your commander, it's always a threat.

The rest of your deck is not so resilient to a board wipe - and a board wipe can seriously set you back, though you can usually hold up a counterspell or two to protect your ninja army. Yuriko makes for a top budget commander deck too - little unblockable guys don't tend to cost too much.

Gamechangers for a Yuriko deck

  • Force of Will
  • Consecrated Sphinx
  • Cyclonic Rift

Sauron, The Dark Lord

A six-cost commander in Grixis, a color combo not exactly known for ramp, is a tough sell. However, if you can hang on and play Sauron, the Dark Lord, you're all set to have a great time. He's a self-fueling engine.

Once Sauron comes down, he starts to roll an unstoppable boulder at your opponent. No one wants to pay the ward cost to get rid of him, and every time anyone casts a spell, you get another Amass trigger.

Soon, your Orcs will be enormous, something on your board will be very hard to block, and you'll be drawing several cards a turn. Sauron works great with several cards from the Lord of the Rings set, which have a very high power level. And you can bring in all the old Amass cards from War of the Spark, too.

He can also reliably pitch your hand into your graveyard, which can make a good setup for graveyard strategies - whether you're trying to get an Underworld Breach / Lion's Eye Diamond loop going for a combo, or just want to reanimate something huge.

Gamechangers for a Sauron deck

  • Demonic Tutor
  • Lion's Eye Diamond
  • Underworld Breach

The Ur Dragon

The Ur Dragon offers a simple strategy, but it's still powerful enough to stampede casual commander tables (and steal a few more competitive wins, too). Its Eminence keyword means that, whether this card is on the battlefield or not, all your MTG dragons are one mana cheaper. The plan should be clear from here - fill your deck with huge, hard-hitting fliers and let rip.

The Ur Dragon is very expensive to get on the battlefield. However, it's a 10/10 flyer that allows you to draw cards equal to the number of your attacking dragons. Even better, you can then place a permanent from your hand onto the battlefield for free.

There are plenty of cards that synergize with The Ur Dragon's matter-of-fact battle plan. Prioritize those that give you extra benefits for playing dragons onto the battlefield or that can make these mana-hungry creatures even cheaper. You'll also need a solid ramp plan if you want your enormous dragons to get off the ground.

Gamechangers for The Ur Dragon

  • Mana Vault
  • Ancient Tomb
  • Chrome Mox

Kaalia Of The Vast

Kaalia of the Vast has been considered a top commander almost since the format's inception. Even today, this card's powers are impressive. Kaalia is a four-cost Mardu commander with flying and the ability to add a card from your hand to the battlefield whenever she attacks. That card must be an Angel, Demon, or Dragon creature, and it's automatically tapped and attacking along with Kaalia.

This is a ferociously fast way to cheat flying threats onto the field. If you can give Kaalia haste, your chosen commander can start handing out freebies as early as turn four. Lightning Greaves, Swiftwood Boots, and Dragon Tempest are your friend here.

Naturally, you'll want a deck full of angels, demons, and dragons to back Kaalia up. You should also leave space for problem-solving cards. Kaalia is a veteran of the competitive commander scene, so you can expect many players to have a game plan when she shows up - removal, removal, and removal.

Gamechangers for a Kaalia of the Vast deck

  • Teferi's Protection
  • Demonic Tutor
  • Imperial Seal


Lathril, Blade Of The Elves

As one of the oldest and best-established creature types in all of Magic: The Gathering, elves have long been a super powerful tribe. There's just been so much time for Wizards to print good elves, and there are now so many of them standing around pouting and hugging trees that it's almost too easy to make a strong elves deck. Just find the cards with the pointy ears and chuck a bunch in.

Lathril, Blade of the Elves is a Kaldheim commander who provides a nice bit of edge for elves decks by adding black to their color identity. This top commander also gives you a powerful new win condition, letting you use your elvish army to drain your opponents for huge chunks of life.

Lathril gives you plenty of options. You can build her to be a classic green elves deck, which ramps up quickly to a critical mass of creatures and then pulls out one of umpteen win conditions. But you can also create a combo style deck that relies on untappers to build up infinite mana, or uses them with Lathril herself to close out the game.

Gamechangers for Lathril

  • Natural Order
  • Survival of the Fittest
  • Gaea's Cradle

Pantlaza, Sun-Favored

Open the door, get on the floor, and prepare to walk the dinosaur, with one of the most popular MTG commanders of recent years. There's a good reason Pantlaza Sun-Favored sees so much play. Coming out of one of the best precon decks ever released, this raptor is a top commander choice if you just want to throw around some big stompy dinosaurs.

Pantlaza's Discover ability means that each dinosaur you cast has the potential to trigger a cascade, letting you fetch up one or potentially more other random dinosaurs from your deck (worst case scenario you hit a mana rock or something). It feels great to start a turn with just your commander on board, and end it with a herd of colossal reptiles whose approaching roars tell your opponents that you are very much the threat. Just make sure you pack enough ramp!

The randomness of this ability might be frustrating to some, but for others it'll ensure their deck always feels fresh.

Gamechangers for Pantlaza

  • Teferi's Protection
  • Farewell
  • Gaea's Cradle

Shroofus Sproutsire

We're not sure if Shroofus Sproutsire truly deserves to be on a list of all-time top commanders, but we've included him as an added extra because we couldn't bear to upset the lil' guy. He's certainly one of the best Jumpstart 2025 Commanders at any rate.

You're always going to have to put a bit of work in to land a hit with this commander, but once you get the ball rolling it's going to move very very fast. While he'd probably work better as Slimefoot's right hand man, this creature will feel like having Scute Swarm in your command zone.

Gamechangers for Shroofus Sproutshire

  • Gaea's Cradle
  • Natural Order
  • Seedborn Muse

Atraxa, Grand Unifier

Alright, Atraxa, Grand Unifier comes with an eye-watering mana cost, and it doesn't have the explosive proliferate powers of our other favored Atraxa commander. However, Grand Unifier offers heaps of power and versatility.

This is a mighty 7/7 commander with flying, vigilance, deathtouch, and lifelink. If you can keep Atraxa in play, it'll obliterate opposing forces, dole out enormous chunks of commander damage, and keep you well-defended in the meantime.

Perhaps more important is Atraxa's enters-the-battlefield ability. This allows you to reveal ten cards from the top of your library. For each card type among those, you can put one card of each revealed type into your hand. The rest go on the bottom of your library in a random order.

This is a commander with fairly generic powers that can feel a bit 'jack of all trades, master of none'. However, this also makes Atraxa suitable for a variety of deck types, from Blink to Phyrexian Typal.

Gamechangers for Atraxa, Grand Unifier

  • Thassa's Oracle
  • Grand Arbiter Augustin IV
  • Force of Will

Brewing a new deck and need to troubleshoot it? Or just want to share your latest creation? We're always keen to find out what nerds are up to in the Wargamer Discord community. And to keep up to date with the latest news and features about everything tabletop, make sure you're subscribed to the Wargamer newsletter.

title: Tabletop Battles Hobby Round-Up: July 2026
content:
We're more than halfway through the year, when priming becomes impossible for most of us because it's too humid and vacations abound. Indeed, a bunch of us got to see everyone's recent projects in-person in Linthicum Heights at the 2026 Goonhammer Open, or in Tacoma for the Tacoma Warhammer Open where Rob won a Golden Ticket! So let's see what the crew has been up to in the hobby mines in between tearing the tournament circuit up from coast to coast!

Jack

With the Tacoma Open mid-month, I needed to update some of my long-untouched Blood Angels to avoid just running the same Imperial Fist army every single year/edition.

Blood Angels Sanguinary Guard. Credit: Jack Hunter

I started off with finally finishing six Sanguinary Guard. I started on these in 2024 when they released and never got past the primer stage, but now that I've finished them I really love them.

Blood Angels Death Company. Credit: Jack Hunter

After that was another five Death Company. I already had five done, but it seems like 10-man squads are the way to go here - so I slammed out another five to fill them up.

Chaplain Lemartes. Credit: Jack Hunter

And finally I had to get Lemartes done to go with them. I don't love what I did on his right shoulder pad, and may go back in to brighten it up some more, but he's a fun model (and horny with the spiked garter and ball gag). After Tacoma I took a few days off from painting to recover from cramming these out, and am very nearly done with another six Sanguinary Guard before I move on to the Armageddon box.

Rockfish

I think I'll probably be part of a theme for this particular month of mostly working on stuff from the Armageddon box, thought I am super close to being done it with only ten models left! Let me kick off with the marine side...

Intercessors. Credit: Rockfish

Eradicators with Heavy Bolters. Credit: Rockfish

Land Speeder. Credit: Rockfish

Land Speeder. Credit: Rockfish

Beyond the marines I also did the remainder of the boyz and about half the ork characters!

Ork Boyz. Credit: Rockfish

Warboss. Credit: Rockfish

Bigboss. Credit: Rockfish

Painboy. Credit: Rockfish

NotThatHenryC

Ok well it's true that I've made a start on some Armageddon stuff. I've been working on some reinforcements for the Crimson Fist army I started back in 8th edition, which I've done both with the Armageddon stuff and by attacking the vast pile of grey plastic shame that has accumulated.

The sensible thing would be to pick a unit and get it finished. I haven't quite done that. Here's what I'm working on at the moment. A couple of dreadnoughts and speeders are nearly done. I'm doing some details and markings, like the checks on the Ballistus and go-faster stripes on the speeders. There'll be more of that sort of thing to come, plus some transfers. I also need to figure out how I'm basing all this stuff.

Loading...

I'm also building some stuff. I'd done a Pedro Kantor conversion before but the Armageddon Captain is a bit closer to the old metal one. I have assembled a new version using that body as a base, with new arms and some different details - most of which are fists. There's still some Green Stuff work to do, like adding a scroll to the top of the banner.

WIP Pedro Kantor conversion. Credit: NotThatHenryC

I'm making a unit of Sternguard to go with Pedro. I wanted them to look less formal and more dynamic than the standard models so these are made from Assault Intercessor bodies with various bits stuck to them. These are my two Heavy Bolter guys, with guns from Devastators and shields from Inceptors.

WIP Sternguard. Credit: NotThatHenryC

Meanwhile I've been having a lot of fun making terrain for the new Exodite expansion for Kill Team. The expansion has templates to make various structures from plasticard, which is pretty unusual these days. Kill Team has provided us with all sorts of narrative terrain lately but all as models, not designs to scratch build yourself. It makes a change though, and is a nice alternative as a way to produce a low-cost board.

So far I've made these three structures from plasticard. They took a while to build and just a few minutes to paint, using Montana Marble spray over a Colour Forge green, then finished with a green glaze.

Maiden World terrain. Credit: NotThatHenryC

The slideshow below shows the steps to building them. It's pretty laborious but I think the result is very nice.

Loading...

I've managed to order a copy of Exodite, which was not guaranteed as numbers seem to have been very small. My Forest will be populated by Eldar, Dinosaurs and Orks before too long. For now, they've had some extremely old Rangers and Striking Scorpions facing up against some warbikes, which might show their scale at least.

Maiden World terrain. Credit: NotThatHenryC

Contemptor Kevin Stillman

I too got a start on my Armageddon Box, successfully assembling every model in it but only finishing up 10 of them (So a smidge under 20% of the box finished).  I finished:

A unit of Intercessors!  Easily my favorite Space Marine unit from the Armageddon box in everything but engineering (that would be the Land Speeder), these guys were a joy:

Intercessors: Credit, Contemptor Kevin Stillman

In an effort to not fall into a painting rut, I've decided to swap between my Orks and Space Marines in painting this box, after knocking out my favorite two models from the box (the Wartrakk and the Banner Nob).  So the next five were...five Ork Boyz!

Ork Boyz. Credit: Contemptor Kevin Stillman

Jefferson Powers

I didn't get a lot of painting done this month, and what I did was a mixed bag of different things. First up we have a handful of Marvel Crisis Protocol characters:

Image credit: Jefferson Powers

Man-Thing in particular was pretty easy but surprisingly fun to do. Next up we have the big man himself, the Kingpin of Crime.

Image credit: Jefferson Powers

I painted the suit by drybrushing light grey and then white, then did all the details with Speedpaints -- it worked pretty well and went very quickly.

Image credit: Jefferson Powers

This maintenance crew is made by Crooked Dice for their excellent Colony 87 range. I have a fairly large pile of their models that I like to work on in between larger projects. Since I'm not trying to match established characters or game artwork, I can be a little more creative with the color choices.

Image credit: Jefferson Powers

Finally we have Solomon Kane himself, from Monolith's Solomon Kane RPG Vault, a bargain-priced repackaging of the models from their Solomon Kane board game. Since I don't have a particular purpose in mind for them, this is another set of models I'm doing a little at a time as the mood strikes me.

Text about their Paint JOb

Badusernametag

July has been a thicc and delicious month for some of us at TTB, as we sunk our teeth into the brand roving new Ogor Mawtribes boxed set! Such lovely models and as a long time Ogor/Ogre player and MawFanatic this was a special treat.

I painted some droogs and a Tyrant for the review/ Battletome article and smashed the Ironguts together. Didn’t get the Cav done yet, but they’re coming soon. As I’m working on that Beastclaw force I never knew was quite to my taste...

Ogor Tyrant
Credit: @badusernametag

Back with a new batch!?
Ogor Gluttons and Tyrant
Credit: @badusernametag

Ogor Gluttons
Credit: @badusernametag

Ogor Gluttons
Credit: @badusernametag

Ogor Gluttons
Credit: @badusernametag

Ogor Gluttons
Credit: @badusernametag

Ogor Gluttons
Credit: @badusernametag

Ogor Ironguts
Credit: @badusernametag

Ogor Gluttons
Credit: @badusernametag

Then I gave an all time favourite Ogre a little 10 minute (literally) paint job from 2021 a glow up...

10 minute paint job!!
Credit: @badusernametag

To be a little bit cooler with a 2 hour 2026 paint job! Much nicer, meaner!

80’s Ogre- ’26 paint job in oils.
Credit: @badusernametag

80’s Ogre- ’26 paint job in oils.
Credit: @badusernametag

Two old friends
Credit: @badusernametag

Finally I added another LineOrc, ‘Porcchetta’ to Da Orgheim Oinkers, my Orc Bloodbowl team. Who are currently in second position in the Bawdy Auld Lundenwic Stunners SAAFFF division! Fun!

Remember kids, better to be a PIG, than an ELF?!?

Orgheim Oinkers-
“I’d rather be a PIG, than an ELF!!!”
Credit: @badusernametag

SRM

This was a light month for hobby, but a big month for games played. Fortunately you can catch up on that over on the 40k Badcast, where we recapped the Tacoma Open, our first GT of 11th edition 40k.

Ultramarines Librarian in Terminator Armor. Credit: SRM

I went hard on Librarians this month, as Librarius Conclave became the new hotness for a brief flash of time. First among these was the Terminator Librarian from Leviathan, and with him done, I can finally mark that box complete, some three years late. I found all the runic engraving to be kind of a pain to paint in and around, and if you look closely it probably isn't as clean as I'd like. It was nice working some different colors in there though, pivoting to an aqua color for the gems and force weapon, plus the little runnels of psychic energy on his armor. I probably should have done those in purple instead, but it's good enough for the studio paintjobs so it's probably good enough for mine.

Ultramarines Librarian. Credit: SRM

One big box down and we're on to the next! The Armageddon Librarian was a fun model to paint, with some lovely expanses of fabric to layer up. He had more of those engraved details that I don't super enjoy, plus the psychic doodaddery on his staff is kind of annoying, but I'm happy with the result. He's a pretty hard model to carry around in a case though, sticking out in seemingly every dimension. It's also strange batch painting a quartet of extremely detailed character models, but such is life in the Warhammer mines.

Ultramarines Librarian. Credit: SRM

I'd picked up the Ultramarines Combat Patrol with the intent of kitbashing Tigurius with a regular Librarian, and that's exactly what I ended up doing. A little shaving on the arm nubs made it an easy conversion, but I didn't go wild on more converting or the paintjob, as he's just got so much stuff on him. I like painting force swords and axes more than force staves, it just gives a better canvas for those big long blends and lends more color to the model. If you couldn't tell, I very much enjoy going hard with color. Unfortunately a smidge of black weathering powder wandered over from his back vents to the skull on his head then got sealed with varnish, so I'll have to paint over that someday.

Ultramarines Librarian. Credit: SRM

For the last of this batch of Librarians, I painted the other half of the Tigurius/vanilla Librarian kitbash process. Despite being made up of mostly leftover pieces, I still like this guy. Most importantly, he incorporates Li'l Baby Stabbums from the old plastic Librarian model. My buddy Mason got that model back in like 2013 and gave me the cherub, and I've just been waiting over a decade for the right model to use him on. I intended to stick him on the Armageddon Librarian (itself a soft remake of that older Librarian model) but the directions of the fabric didn't line up, so instead he's here on this more up-and-down space wizard.

Ultramarines Sternguard with Heavy Bolters. Credit: SRM

Part of what made Librarius so good was how well it paired with Sternguard, and my Veteran Intercessors from 8th served admirably as Sternguard stand-ins. That old unit didn't have access to any of the cool toys Sternguard have now that they've gotten the Primaris treatment, so I painted up a pair of Heavy Bolters to bring them up to speed. Naturally these were finished too late to bring to the Tacoma Open, but they're here now, and I've been told that late is better than never, though I can't find a source on that particular clai. These guys were an easy kitbash using the Heavy Bolter from the Space Marine Heroes Gravis Marine and Sicarius' spare head for one guy, and standard Sternguard bits for the other, given to me by my buddy Nik. Like the models you've seen in this article, we are kitbashes of all the bits we've been given in our lives, be they plastic or something more substantial.

With the brief period of Librarius dominance likely at an end, it's time to move on to other, likely still blue things. I'm giving Reclamation Force a try these days, and that'll mean painting more regular jamokes to flesh out my Assault Intercessor squads. There's some old army modernization to get to for sure, though I'll probably be distracted by something new and shiny before I can get all my squads up to speed. While I typically reject the "Dug from Up" characterization of having ADHD, that new XCOM game I got to interview Chris from Modiphius about sure has my interest, and Necromunda is getting some love, so we might be near the end of Ultramarines season.

dirtboi

My stuff consists of Star Wars: Legion minis! Been plugging away at the new Mandalorian Army box since the release and even finished some Initiates for a HTPE found here. Tried a "friends pick your colors" experiment with these fellas but wasn't too satisfied with some of the layering colors I selected. Still, I am quite please and looking forward to the next batch.

Picture credit: dirtboi

I also finished up my Armorer for another HTPE that releases next week, and I tried out some Vallejo True Metallic Metals, specifically the Forge Red and the Imperial Gold ranges. Quite loving these metallics, going to definitely pick up more. Here she is hanging out with some of her Children of the Watch Initiates.

Picture credit: dirtboi

Also plugged away at my "sizeable" Ohnaka Gang army, getting ever so closer to the finish line. By "sizeable", I mean 4 BIG tanks. I still need to oil wash the tanks, bases, and anything metallic, apply some weathering, and finish with a nice black base rim. It would help if I stopped going to small local tournaments and dedicated that 10 hours to crossing said finish line.

Loading...

Andrew_N

Ive been bit bad by the Battletech bug this month - I finished a light company's worth of 2nd Free Worlds Guards just this week, and instead of focusing on terrain or models for Heresy or Old World next, all I want to do is paint more mechs!   I likely will be painting some Rasalhague Dominion next, or perhaps some Avalon Hussars from the Federated Sons. I should finish painting some more Solar Auxilia, though!

2nd Free Worlds Guards. Credit: Andrew_N Have any questions or feedback? Drop us a note in the comments below or email us at contact@tabletopbattles.com. Want articles like this linked in your inbox every Monday morning? Sign up for our newsletter. And don't forget that you can support us on Patreon for backer rewards like early video content, Administratum access, an ad-free experience on our website, and subscriber-only content covering competitive Warhammer 40K!

title: Warhammer 40k codex release dates for 11th edition - news and FAQs
content:
Games Workshop has revealed that the first 11th edition Warhammer 40k codex will be for the Orks - and some very intriguing changes are coming for these critical rulebooks. Read on for Wargamer's complete 11th edition codex tracker, updated regularly with all the latest news about codex release dates, plus key FAQs to understand how your old 10th edition codexes work in the new edition.

If you're new to Games Workshop's premier sci-fi miniature wargame, our expert guide to the Warhammer 40k factions will help you get oriented in this huge sci-fi world. And for all the info on the upcoming new version of the game, read our complete rundown on Warhammer 40k 11th Edition.

  • Upcoming codex news
  • 10th Edition codex release dates
  • How to redeem digital codexes
  • FAQ

Upcoming 11th Edition codexes

The Orks will get the first new codex for Warhammer 40k 11th edition. Games Workshop announced that the greenskins had made it to the front of the queue during the Big Summer Preview on June 26, though the firm hasn't yet revealed the release date for the new book. We'd originally expected it by early August, but at this stage - based on the timing of other, known releases - we predict the Orks 11e codex will drop right at the end of August 2026.

The Ork codex will form the template for the new edition. One interesting change that GW has announced is that the 'dex is going to feature 15 detachments. That's a lot of Warhammer 40k detachments - our best guess is that they'll lean away from the big whole-army detachments of 10th edition, and have many smaller detachments you can build like a smorgasbord.

The new codex will have "a new 'Collecting' section giving advice for building Ork armies in four distinct archetypes", and will feature "in-depth information about all of the faction's units with the return of bestiary-style lore entries".

A code in the back of the codex will provide access to the rules in the Warhammer 40k app, but this will now include "quarterly drops of rules and lore all the way through the edition… including extra detachments and other rules".

GW has confirmed that 10th edition codexes will remain valid until each faction's new book comes along - as opposed to being replaced with temporary index rules, as we saw at 10th edition's launch in 2023.

Locking rules to codexes remains frustrating. For many fans, a codex's essential game rules, lore, art, and tips makes it worth the $60 price tag. But official balance updates are now so frequent that the printed rules are out of date before anyone can use them - leading many to see codexes as merely a very expensive unlock code to get their army rules from the app, where balance updates are applied live (or at least, something like live).

10th Edition codex release dates

The most recent new Warhammer 40k Codex was Codex: Drukhari, which went up for pre-order on September 27, 2025, and released on October 11.

Of the at least 27 10th edition codexes we expected to arrive over the (roughly) three years of the edition, a whopping 30 factions now have either a codex or an updated index. This includes a re-release of Index Deathwatch - which was briefly deprecated by Codex Imperial Agents - and mid-edition refreshes of both Index Chaos Daemons and Index Imperial Knights.

How do I redeem Warhammer 40k codex codes?

You'll find a unique Warhammer 40k codex code in the back of each printed Codex. You can register this code on your MyWarhammer account, which will in turn unlock all the datasheets and Detachments from the Codex in the Warhammer 40k app.

You can then use that data in the Battle Forge army builder. You will be limited to just one army list at a time in the app, unless you also have a Warhammer+ subscription.

Warhammer 40k codexes FAQ

Codexes are bread and butter to long time Warhammer 40,000 fans; we know what they're for, we know how they change the game, and boy oh boy do we know how much they cost.

But if you're new to the hobby, the whole concept of them can be a bit bewildering. The idea of needing another rulebook, on top of the actual rulebook, is tough enough - but buying a new one every three years? It's one of the rougher parts of the 40k hobby, and it bears a bit of explanation. Here's what codexes are, how they work, how to use them, and how they may change in the future.

What is a Warhammer 40k codex?

Alongside the core rules for Warhammer 40k, each army has its own codex where you'll find rules for all its units, the army-wide rules that give it a distinctive character, and other options you can choose from when you construct a list. They also contain artwork, lore, stories, and examples of painted armies.

What do you use the codex for in games?

During a game of Warhammer 40k - especially when you're new to the game or learning a new faction - you'll need to refer to your army's codex frequently to check its rules.

Most importantly, you need to know the stats for each unit, its weapons, and abilities. For example, you'll find yourself double checking how many inches it can move each turn, the range and power of its shooting attacks, or how effective its armor is at preventing damage. Over time, you'll know more and more of those key numbers from memory - but it's important to have the codex on hand to double check, so you don't accidentally cheat!

Codexes are also super important before the game, as they include the different Detachments you can choose for your army. These are army building choices which shape your game plan by applying different army wide buffs, as well as specialized abilities to trigger at crucial moments during the game.

Can I buy a digital or PDF version of my codex?

No, Games Workshop doesn't sell PDF versions of codexes. Since the launch of the official Warhammer 40k app in July 2020, the only official, GW supported way to view a codex's rules in digital form is to buy a copy of the physical book, then redeem its unique code to unlock it inside the app. We've written instructions on doing that - see above.

Prior to 2020, new 40k codex books were available in both printed physical and ebook formats. They were never sold as PDFs, so any codex PDF you encounter online is likely to be an unauthorized pirate copy.

How do Games Workshop's codex release dates work?

During each three year long 'edition' of Warhammer 40k, GW normally releases one new codex for each playable army in the game. Typically, they're released in groups of one or two, once every two months or so.

How and when these codexes are released can vary, depending on how fundamentally the current 'edition' has hanged the game's core rules. Because 10th Edition changed the core rules significantly in 2023, GW completely retired all 9th Edition codexes from the game, and provided a full set of free 'index' rules for each army, for fans to play with until their army's new full codex arrived.

As codexes were released, they superceded the indexes, updating rules and points, and adding new detachments that provided different ways to build an army that complete with with new abilities, enhancements, stratagems.

What about old codexes - can I use those?

As soon as an army's latest Warhammer 40k codex is released, the previous edition's rules are no longer valid in 'Matched Play' games. That means tournaments and organized play in general will always use the most up to date codex rules, and all earlier books are no longer usable.

However, many players enjoy running games of older editions, deliberately using the rules from previous editions' core rules and codexes, to play the game 'as it was then'. Your old codexes might not be tournament legal, but they don't simply disappear!

Got a burning question about your codex? You'll find a friendly and helpful community in the Wargamer Discord. To keep up with the latest news about upcoming codex releases, subscribe to the Wargamer newsletter.

title: Disney Villainous expansion guide
content:
There are currently eight Disney Villanous expansions, each filled with a total of 20 dastardly do-badders. After the base game was such a hit, it's no wonder board game fans wanted more evil options to control. This guide explains what's inside all Disney Villainous expansions, as well as how complex, fun, and beginner friendly they are.

Disney Villainous is a solid gold classic, though it doesn't quite make our list of the best board games of all time. Playing as the bad guy is compelling in itself, and what better villain is there than a cartoon villain?

All Disney Villainous expansions:

  • Wicked to the Core
  • Evil Comes Prepared
  • Perfectly Wretched
  • Despicable Plots
  • Bigger and Badder
  • Introduction to Evil
  • Filled with Fright
  • Sugar and Spite
  • On Treacherous Tides
  • Disney Villainous Unstoppable
  • Success at Any Cost
  • Come, We Fly
  • Darkness Brewing

What's in a Disney Villainous expansion?

Most of the currently available expansions adds three fully playable villains to the game, with their own win conditions, Villain decks, and Fate decks. However, newer releases only add one or two. Here's a handy table breaking down which villains each expansion includes before we dive into detail:

Expansion New playable villains
Wicked to the Core
  • The Evil Queen (Snow White)
  • Hades (Hercules)
  • Dr. Facilier (The Princess and the Frog)
Evil Comes Prepared
  • Scar (The Lion King)
  • Ratigan ( The Great Mouse Detective)
  • Yzma (The Emperor's New Groove)
Perfectly Wretched
  • Cruella De Vil (101 Dalmatians)
  • Mother Gothel (Tangled)
  • Pete (Steamboat Willie)
Despicable Plots
  • Gaston (Beauty and the Beast)
  • The H0rned King (The Black Cauldron)
  • Wicked Stepmother / Lady Tremaine (Cinderella)
Bigger and Badder
  • Syndrome (The Incredibles)
  • Lotso (Toy Story 3)
  • Madame Mim (The Sword in the Stone)
Introduction to Evil
  • None (repackaged base set)
Filled With Fright
  • Oogie Boogie (Nightmare Before Christmas)
Sugar and Spite
  • Shere Kahn (The Jungle Book)
  • King Candy (Wreck It Ralph)
Treacherous Tides
  • Davy Jones (Pirates of the Caribbean)
  • Tamatoa (Moana)
Disney Villainous Unstoppable
  • None (repackaged standalone game)
Success at Any Cost
  • Ernesto de la Cruz (Coco)
  • Prince Hans (Frozen)
Come, We Fly
  • Sanderson Sisters (Hocus Pocus)
Darkness Brewing
  • Sanderson Sisters (Hocus Pocus)
  • Maleficent (Sleeping Beauty)
  • Evil Queen (Snow White)
  • Ursula (The Little Mermaid)

Disney Villainous: Wicked to the Core

The first Disney Villainous expansion, Wicked to the Core, has Hades, Snow White's Evil Queen, and Dr. Facilier from The Princess and the Frog. It has an eclectic mix of mechanics and difficulty levels. Hades is all about movement and must bring the Titans over to ransack Olympus, while Evil Queen acts alone as a one-woman killing machine, vanquishing heroes by brewing nasty potions.

Dr Facilier meanwhile, turns the game into a deckbuilding board game with his complex mechanics, which involve putting cards in a separate 'Fortune' deck. He's tough to get a handle on, so while this was the first Disney Villainous Expansion ever released, and has some of the most fun heroes, it's a little wonky in both balance and complexity and might not be the one to start with.

Disney Villainous: Evil Comes Prepared

Only at Villainous Expansion #2, Evil Comes Prepared, and they're already breaking out Ratigan from The Great Mouse Detective, who features here alongside fan-favorite Scar, and Yzma from The Emperor's New Groove. This is probably the best Disney Villainous expansion for beginner board gamers.

Yzma has to search for Kuzco in four different Fate decks, Scar's just gotta beat up a load of heroes, and Ratigan has a fun gimmick in that his first objective can be thwarted, in which case he has to defeat the main hero as a backup plot. All unique takes on the game, but nothing too crazy.

Disney Villainous: Perfectly Wretched

Villainous Expansion 3 - Perfectly Wretched - features Cruella De Vil, Mother Gothel, and Pete from Steamboat Willie (the first Mickey Mouse cartoon). Each Disney Villainous: Perfectly Wretched character has its own unique playstyle, but none are overly complex, making this another good get for beginners to the series or younger boardgamers.

Pete's game board and cards are all in black and white, adding a nice bit of style - plus his game plan is always different. You randomly choose four out of five goals each game, keeping your objectives hidden from the other players. Mother Gothel has a nice risk/reward game where your aim is to build up Rapunzel's trust, and Cruella just wants to hoover up a ton of puppy tokens.

Disney Villainous: Despicable Plots

Villainous Expansion 4 - Despicable Plots - features Gaston, and then two oddballs, The Horned King from Black Cauldron and the Wicked Stepmother (actual name Lady Tremaine) from Cinderella. As well as having less star power than many of the other Villainous expansions, Despicable Plots has some fiddly mechanics that may prove frustrating. It's by no means bad, and each villain has something interesting going on, if you can pull it off, but in our view - not the place to start.

Disney Villainous: Bigger and Badder

Despite the 'bigger' in Bigger and Badder, there are still only three characters in Villainous Expansion 5. This time we're breaking into Pixar land with Syndrome from The Incredibles and Lotso from Toy Story 3, alongside the witchy Madame Mim from The Sword in the Stone.

A very colorful expansion, Mim is the surprise standout here, requiring you to defeat Merlin in a more complex version of Rock Paper Scissors that represents the film's transformation battle (the only part of the movie most people remember).

Disney Villainous: Introduction to Evil

A revamped (streamlined?) version of the original box, but with some of the villains missing, Introduction to Evil is a Disney Villainous game intended for new players, not yet used to the devious world of plotting and planning. It offers a couple of very minor rules changes, and a lower price point, and it's up to you if that makes up for taking two of the (more enjoyable, in our opinion) villains out of the base game.

Disney Villainous: Filled with Fright

Disney Villainous' first single character expansion, Filled with Fright, lets you play as Oogie Boogie from Nightmare Before Christmas. Your mission is to defeat Jack and take his place on the throne as Pumpkin King.

This expansion released for Halloween in October 2023. Oogie is a gambling ghoul, and the expansion comes with dice that play into many of the villain's cards.

It's worth noting that, as the box comes with just one villain, this is the first Disney Villainous expansion that doesn't work as a standalone game. Don't buy it for someone who isn't already a Villainous fan.

Disney Villainous: Sugar and Spite

In 2024, Disney Villainous switched to a new release strategy that resulted in cheaper expansions, although it meant they would only hold two villains rather than three. The first of these was Sugar and Spite, which featured Wreck It Ralph's King Candy and Shere Khan from Jungle Book.

King Candy has a race track rather than realms to move across, which shakes up the tactics of a standard Villainous game. This adds a level of complexity that might put off newbies to the board game, but it keeps things delightfully fresh for veterans.

Shere Khan is a simpler, more traditional villain, but that doesn't mean he's at a disadvantage. He simply needs to defeat Mowgli and keep fire away from his board, a clear win condition that can be achieved surprisingly quickly - meaning the King Candy player must stay on their toes.

Treacherous Tides

Released on July 21, 2025, Disney Villainous expansion 8 features the game's first live action villain. And it's a strong one: the tentacled, crab-clawed Pirates of the Caribbean character Davy Jones strikes an imposing figure (and makes for a very recognizable silhouette) on the front of the box.

Treacherous Tides is another two-character expansion, establishing this as the norm going forwards. It's got a nautical theme, as Tamatoa, the giant crab monster from Moana, features alongside The Flying Dutchman's captain.

Both characters are hunting for treasure here. Davy Jones' mission involves collecting five treasure tokens, while Tamatoa's requires finding Maui's Hook and the Heart of Te Fiti in your villain deck, and getting them to his lair. Classic Villainous stuff, really!

Disney Villainous Unstoppable

Released in staggered fashion between August and October 2025, Disney Villainous Unstoppable is a spinoff that reworks the base mechanics and early villains of the series, all on a shared board. Instead of playing asymmetric roles, everyone uses the same rules to control one or more iconic Disney villains.

It's a two-to-four-player game that promises to be a punchier, more approachable version of the original Disney Villainous. Hades, Ursula, Maleficent, and Scar return to star, with broadly reworked mechanics designed to give the same overall Villainous experience, but using simpler rules to make things more accessible for youngsters.

Success At Any Cost

While Frozen is a pop-culture giant, Coco's Ernesto de la Cruz is certainly a bigger villain personality compared to the forgettable Prince Hans, so it's no surprise that the skeleton is the face of this July 2026 Villainous release.

The two have quite different objectives. The Coco villain is trying to flip photo cards face down to cover up his crimes and doom poor Hector. Meanwhile, the twist-villain prince wants to freeze locations, then flip the board, then freeze more locations before defeating Anya and Elsa.

It seems like Hans has slightly more to do, but more powerful card and engine components to make up for his tough objective.

Come, We Fly

Another live action Villainous expansion dropped in late July 2026. Another single villain box with a Halloween feel, Come, We Fly obviously can't be played standalone, but Villainous devotees who were around in the 90s might not care, since they now have the opportunity to put the Sanderson Sisters from Hocus Pocus into their game.

With Come, We Fly you play all three of the witches together, and these characters have lots of synergies and tricks that involve the trio working together. Your objective is to complete and use the Life potion, completing a recipe-style list of somewhat convoluted objectives.

Darkness Brewing

A witch-themed Villainous set also released alongside Come, We Fly, and it represents much better value for money if you don't already own most of the characters. You get the new Hocus Pocus villains, plus Malificent, Evil Queen, and Ursula: all three being absolute bangers.

Do you need the base Disney Villainous Game?

Nope! Pretty much every Disney Villainous expansion can be played on its own, and they're also all compatible with each other. You can take any Disney Villainous game in your collection and mix and muddle it up with any other expansion, and still have a grand old time.

That said, the base Disney Villainous game touts an impressive six heroes, compared to the three found in expansions. Purely in terms of bang for your buck, you may be well served by picking up the bigger, original box.

If you're sold on Villainous by the gameplay as much as the theme, you might also enjoy our guide to the Marvel Villainous expansions. Alternatively, you can always drop into the free Wargamer Discord community and chat with us about your fave expansions and villains - or which classic Disney movies should get the Villainous treatment next!

title: MTG Arena codes for August 2026
content:
MTG Arena codes are an essential, mostly free kick-start for your digital collection, unlocking new Magic: The Gathering cards, booster packs, XP, and cosmetic items like card sleeves, avatars, and more. Read on to find all working MTGA codes in 2026, as well as full instructions on how to redeem promo codes on PC and mobile.

Each month, as the MTG release schedule rolls on, we trawl Wizards' announcements about new MTG sets to update this list, telling you which codes currently work; which have expired; and which brand-new codes have sprung up for the game. The good news is that you can still unlock free cards to boost your MTG Arena decks.

Here's how to get MTGA codes:

  • All free MTG Arena codes in August 2026
  • Unlock the cabbage companion
  • MTG Arena rewards
  • How to redeem MTG Arena codes
  • Where to find more MTGA codes
  • All expired MTGA codes

All free MTG Arena codes in August 2026

As of August 2026, there are currently no working MTG Arena codes for use on the Arena client.

This is sad news for bargain hunters, but the good news is that you'll still pick up plenty of free packs by playing! 

Unlock the cabbage companion

Would you like to have a high fidelity cabbage for your companion? Of course you would! This nutritious friend is available as a free easter egg, added to celebrate the MTG Avatar: The Last Airbender set in 2025. You can unlock it by playing any matched game on the Avatar battlefield, and clicking on the Cabbage Merchant's card until it explodes. Do this and you'll be rewarded with your very own cabbage.

Is it better than the beachball or the pet rock? That's for you to judge.

MTG Arena rewards

These days, Wizards hands out free booster packs as MTG Arena rewards to celebrate the release of new sets. These arrive directly in your in-game inbox without the need to redeem a code. Plus, new players who complete the how to play tutorial are greeted with a whole stack of reward packs to crack open from the last couple of years' worth of sets (plus a selection of variant land cards to use).

Here are all the rewards each MTG Arena player has access to, as of August 2026:

  • 3 x Alchemy: Strixhaven boosters
  • 3 x Secrets of Strixhaven boosters
  • 3 x Alchemy: Lorwyn boosters
  • 3 x Lorwyn: Eclipsed boosters
  • 3 x Avatar: The Last Airbender boosters
  • 3 x Through the Omenpaths boosters
  • 3 x Edge of Eternities boosters
  • 3 x Magic: The Gathering - Final Fantasy boosters
  • 3 x Alchemy: Tarkir boosters
  • 3 x Tarkir: Dragonstorm boosters
  • 3 x Alchemy: Aetherdrift boosters
  • 3 x Aetherdrift boosters
  • 3 x MTG Foundations boosters
  • 3 x Alchemy: Duskmourn boosters
  • 3 x Duskmourn boosters
  • 3 x Bloomburrow boosters
  • 3 x Alchemy: Bloomburrow boosters
  • 3 x Modern Horizons 3 boosters
  • 3 x Lost Caverns of Ixalan boosters
  • 3 x Alchemy: Ixalan boosters
  • 3 x Murders at Karlov Manor boosters
  • 3 x Alchemy: Karlov Manor boosters
  • 3 x Shadows Over Innistrad Remastered boosters
  • 3 x Phyrexia: All Will Be One boosters
  • 3 x Alchemy: Phyrexia boosters
  • 3 x Outlaws of Thunder Junction boosters
  • 3 x Alchemy: Thunder Junction boosters
  • 3 x The Lord of the Rings: Tales of Middle-earth boosters
  • 3 x Wilds of Eldraine boosters
  • 3 x Alchemy: Eldraine boosters
  • 3 x Khans of Tarkir boosters
  • 3 x March of the Machine boosters
  • 3 x March of the Machine: The Aftermath boosters
  • 1 x Basic Wastes Land (from Explorer Anthology 2)
  • 6 x Alchemy: Brothers War boosters

How to redeem MTG Arena codes

There are two ways to redeem MTG Arena codes on PC, and both are dead easy - just pick your method below and follow our step-by-step guide.

How to redeem codes in the Arena client

The most common and simplest way to cash in your codes is directly inside the MTG Arena client. Here's how to do it:

1. Open up the game on PC and click on the 'Store' tab at the top of the page.

2. You'll see a small oval text box in the top right corner, with 'Redeem Code' written inside (we've highlighted it in red in the picture above).

3. Copy your code into the box and hit enter.

4. Your reward automatically appears in your account!

How to redeem codes via your Wizards account

If you'd rather not boot up the game, you can also redeem codes by entering them into your Wizards of the Coast account page. Here's how you do this:

1. Log in using your MTG Arena details, and on the right-hand side of your account dashboard, you'll find a nice, big 'Redeem a code' box.

2. Paste the code inside and click 'Redeem'.

3. The goods will appear in your account next time you log in to the Arena game client.

How to redeem MTGA codes on mobile

If you're primarily a mobile MTGA player and want to redeem codes on your phone, the process can feel a bit more convoluted, because - frustratingly - there's still no way to redeem codes directly through the iOS and Android versions of the game.

The main way to get the job done is simply via mobile web, with the following steps:

  1. Log in to your Wizards account via your mobile browser.
  2. Scroll down to the 'Redeem a Code' box as shown in the image above.
  3. Enter your code, and click 'Redeem'.
  4. Your rewards will show up next time you log into the game.

If everything's worked correctly, you'll see a little green message pop up that reads "Code redeemed successfully", as seen above.

However, if you really want to make things difficult for yourself, you can access that same account-based process from within the MTG Arena mobile client. We don't recommend it, though, because it's janky as all hell - it's far easier just to hop over to your mobile browser and do it there.

Where to find more MTGA codes

If you've already used all the free codes available, and still want to expand your collection of planeswalkers, creatures, and fancy land cosmetics, there are a few other places where you can sometimes get your hands on more MTGA codes to redeem. You can do this either by buying select Magic products that include Arena freebies, or else staying alert for new promo codes and other fans' unused codes shared online.

The main options to try are:

  • Physical Magic: The Gathering products
  • Social media giveaways and competitions
  • Promo codes from local game stores
  • MTG Arena Twitch Prime codes

Physical Magic: The Gathering products

Unlike the Pokémon TCG, not every sealed pack of Magic cards comes with a digital unlock code included - but some physical MTG products do give you a code into the bargain, to grow your digital collection as well as your cardboard mountain. There are three types of products you can buy for this.

Prerelease kits

Wizards of the Coast launches each new Magic: The Gathering set with a pre-release event focused on in-person games in local game stores, selling Prerelease kits of six brand new boosters.

Since 2025, these prerelease kits have no longer included MTG Arena codes packed in the box. Instead, you'll register your Arena account when you attend the pre-release event at a physical store, and your free boosters will appear in your account when you next log in.

However, older prerelease kits can still be found for sale which do contain Arena codes. If you buy one of the following recent Prerelease kits, you can use the included code to unlock MTG Arena boosters for the corresponding set:

Product Reward Approx. Price Link
Murders at Karlov Manor Prerelease kit 6 Arena boosters  $30 Buy at Amazon
Lost Caverns of Ixalan Prerelease kit 6 Arena boosters  $30 Buy at Amazon
Outlaws of Thunder Junction Prerelease kit 6 Arena boosters  $30 Buy at Amazon 
Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate Prerelease kit 6 Arena boosters $47 Buy at Amazon
Kaldheim Prerelease kit 6 Arena boosters $32 Buy at Amazon
Ikoria Prerelease kit 6 Arena boosters $56 Buy at Amazon
Zendikar Rising Prelease kit 6 Arena boosters $27 Buy at Amazon

Starter kits

Starter kits are designed to get newbies into Magic: The Gathering, so they offer up two pre-constructed decks. The kits also come with a code that unlocks each deck in MTG Arena, too.

Buying a second-hand starter kit might mean that your code has already been used, but if you can get one new (or from a reputable, code-selling source), these are the decks to look out for:

  • Bloomburrow Starter Kit
  • Wilds of Eldraine Starter Kit
  • Lord of the Rings Starter Kit
  • Starter Kit 2023
  • Starter Kit 2022
  • Starter Kit 2021
  • Core Set Starter Kit 2021

Planeswalker decks

All physical Planeswalker decks released between the October 2018 set Guilds of Ravnica and Core Set 2021 came with a one-time code to unlock their cards in MTG Arena, so you could use all the same cards online.

Sadly, the older codes from these decks have now expired, and the decks themselves are very difficult to come by (they're all unavailable on Amazon US and UK) - so you'll struggle to find an unopened copy with an intact code for a reasonable price. Even more sadly, free codes isn't a trend that was carried on by the far more available Commander precons.

If you really want the physical cards too, though, it might be worth the hunt; here's the full list of decks with (we think) still functioning codes:

  • Ashiok, Shaper of Fears
  • Basri, Devoted Paladin
  • Chandra, Flame's Catalyst
  • Elspeth, Undaunted Hero
  • Liliana, Death Mage
  • Oko, The Trickster Planeswalker
  • Rowan, Fearless Sparkmage
  • Teferi, Timeless Voyager
  • Vivien's Hunt (released in a Hot Pocket promo)

MTG Arena Secret Lair codes

MTG Arena Secret Lair codes are found in Wizards of the Coast's limited edition, premium Secret Lair boxed sets of one-off collectible cards. The rewards vary, but usually, they unlock exclusive cards and cosmetics.

You can get some pretty sweet, limited edition skins, though - for example, if you bought the 'Warhammer Bundle' during the October 2023 Warhammer 40k Secret Lair, you got two codes, each good for ten premium card sleeves showing the 40k-ified versions of classic cards:

  • Merciless Executioner as "Ork Kommando"
  • Aggravated Assault
  • Krenko, Tin Street Kingpin as "Makari the Lucky Grot"
  • Zurgo Helmsmasher as "Ghazghkull, Prophet of the Waaagh!"
  • Blind Obedience
  • Danitha Capashen, Paragon as "Neave Blacktalon"
  • Najeela, the Blade-Blossom as "Archaeon the Everchosen"
  • Scourge of the Throne as "Stardrake"

Beware, though - this is often the priciest way to find new codes. Each Secret Lair 'drop' can cost anything from $20 to several hundred bucks. We only recommend going this way if you really want the physical cards your codes will come bundled with.

Social media giveaways and competitions

If you're a social media-savvy Magic fan, another way to nab a cheeky extra code is through giveaways or competitions run by major MTG content creators, influencers, or simply kind-hearted fans sharing codes they don't need or want for themselves.

MTGA Codes, a retail website that collects unwanted and unused Arena codes and sells them directly online, regularly runs such giveaways to drive engagement on its Twitter account (@MTGA_CODES).

There's no way to know when such giveaways will take place, or exactly who's going to be doing them - but we can recommend a few creators you should follow just for regular, great content and commentary on Magic and Arena, who have been known to give away MTGA codes in the past:

  • Grzegorz 'Urlich' Kowalski (@urlichmtg) - former Magic Pro League player, Twitch streamer
  • Gerry Thompson (@G3RRYT) - Magic pro player from the US
  • The Asian Avenger (@Theasianavenger) - Magic YouTuber and streamer
  • MTGNerdGirl (@MTGNerdGirl) - Magic YouTuber and streamer

Promo codes from local game stores

It's not all the time, but Wizards of the Coast occasionally creates special MTG Arena codes as part of promoting in-person Magic play through bricks-and-mortar local game stores (LGS). Most recently, it did this via its 'Friday Night Magic At Home' campaign, aimed at helping stores keep regular play events going during Covid lockdowns in 2020.

This isn't a regular occurrence, though, and it's entirely dependent on Wizards' ongoing strategy for working with game stores - if you're angling for extra codes, we'd recommend checking in with the staff at your LGS to see if there's anything on offer.

MTG Arena Twitch Prime codes

In the past, Wizards of the Coast has collaborated with other big brands to offer MTG Arena promo codes as a bonus for their subscribers - and, back in 2019, it gave away free unlock codes as a benefit for the Twitch Prime service (now merged with Amazon Prime Gaming).

All you had to do to get the code was sign into your Twitch Prime account, check the 'Loot' section, click on 'claim', and it would generate a code for you to redeem directly in the Arena client.

Sadly, we haven't seen any more new MTGA codes come through this service in the years since - but there's always a chance, so if you're constantly on the hunt for fresh codes, it's worth periodically checking in on your Prime Gaming account (there's also a bunch of free videogame downloads and other goodies there, of course).

Naturally, we'll also update this guide the moment we see any new MTG Arena unlockables pop up on the platform.

The following expired MTG Arena codes are already dead and gone - if you try to redeem them, you'll get a sad little red error message that reads: "This code is not valid or has already been used the maximum number of times for this account".
